skill.name: assume-cloudformation-role
skill.description: Assume an AWS IAM role for CloudFormation stack operations and export temporary AWS credentials for CLI use.
skill.summary: Prepare temporary AWS credentials for CloudFormation create, update, and delete operations.
skill.author: Daisuke897

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs AWS CLI and jq commands to assume a CloudFormation write role and export temporary AWS credential variables. Most backtick detections are markdown formatting false positives, but the shell command substitution, environment variable export, shared /tmp credential file, and AWS credential directory references are real security concerns that require safer handling.

remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp with restrictive permissions, trap cleanup on exit, or parse the AWS CLI JSON without writing credentials to a shared /tmp path.

remediation.issue: AWS credentials exported into the parent shell environment
remediation.suggestion: Prefer scoped execution, such as running the required CloudFormation command with temporary environment variables only for that process.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded default AWS account role ARN and profile
remediation.suggestion: Require users to confirm or provide the role ARN and profile before running commands that grant CloudFormation write access.

remediation.issue: Credential cleanup depends on the final rm command
remediation.suggestion: Add a shell trap and avoid command tracing so temporary credentials are removed even when an intermediate command fails.

content.value_statement: CloudFormation work often needs short lived role credentials before stack changes can run. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable AWS STS workflow for preparing those credentials.
actual_capabilities: Shows the AWS STS assume-role command for a CloudFormation write role.
Documents default profile, role ARN, and role session name inputs.
Explains how to parse STS credential output with jq.
Exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN for AWS CLI use.
Lists CloudFormation create-stack, update-stack, and delete-stack examples.
States prerequisites for AWS CLI, jq, profile configuration, and AssumeRole permission.
limitations: It does not validate IAM permissions before stack operations begin.
It uses a hardcoded example role ARN and profile that may not match other AWS accounts.
It stores credential JSON in a predictable temporary path in the documented example.
It does not inspect or validate CloudFormation templates.

use_cases.title: Prepare deployment credentials
use_cases.description: Assume a CloudFormation write role before creating or updating a stack from the AWS CLI.

use_cases.title: Standardize role setup
use_cases.description: Give a team a consistent sequence for obtaining temporary AWS credentials before stack maintenance.

use_cases.title: Run controlled stack cleanup
use_cases.description: Set temporary credentials before deleting a known CloudFormation stack during maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Assume the default role
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup with the documented defaults.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the assume-cloudformation-role skill with the default profile and role session name. Explain each command before I run it.

prompt_templates.title: Use a custom AWS profile
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has a different local AWS CLI profile.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill with my AWS CLI profile named staging-admin. Keep the default role session name unless I specify another one.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for a stack update
prompt_templates.scenario: Credentials are needed before a specific CloudFormation change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assume the CloudFormation role, then help me confirm the AWS identity before I run an update-stack command.

prompt_templates.title: Harden the credential workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants safer handling of temporary secrets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the assume-role workflow to avoid a predictable /tmp credential file and keep credentials scoped to one CloudFormation command.

output_examples.input: Assume the CloudFormation write role with the default profile.
output_examples.output: The assistant presents the STS assume-role command, shows how credentials are extracted, and reminds the user to remove temporary credential files.

output: Confirms the AWS profile and role ARN.
Provides the temporary credential setup sequence.
Suggests verifying caller identity before the stack update.

output_examples.input: Make the credential setup safer for a shared workstation.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a unique temporary file, restrictive permissions, trap-based cleanup, and process-scoped environment variables.

best_practices: Verify the AWS account and caller identity before running stack changes.
Use the shortest practical credential lifetime and clear environment variables after use.
Store temporary credential files with restrictive permissions and automatic cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse the hardcoded example role ARN without confirming the target account.
Do not leave AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SESSION_TOKEN exported after the task finishes.
Do not write active credentials to predictable shared paths on multi-user systems.

faq.question: Does this skill create or update CloudFormation stacks by itself?
faq.answer: No. It prepares AWS credentials so a user can run CloudFormation commands afterward.

faq.question: Which AWS permissions are required?
faq.answer: The source profile needs sts:AssumeRole permission for the configured CloudFormation write role.

faq.question: How long do the temporary credentials last?
faq.answer: The skill notes that temporary credentials typically expire after about one hour.

faq.question: Can I use a different role ARN?
faq.answer: Yes. The role ARN is an input parameter and should match your AWS account and deployment policy.

faq.question: Is this safe on a shared machine?
faq.answer: Use caution. The documented example writes credentials to /tmp, so safer temporary file handling is recommended.

faq.question: Does it require jq?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow uses jq to extract fields from the AWS STS JSON response.
